Risk-set weights at the event times

Source: R/utils.R
risk_set_weights.Rd

The risk-set averages \(S^{(k)}\) use the same kernel as the main term of each estimating equation, so they are built from the same weight function and the same one-sided rule, here, rather than rewritten in C++. Rows are the distinct event times among the rows that contribute (delta == 1 and a nonzero row weight), columns are the observation rows, and index maps each data row to its row of K (0-based, -1 for a row that does not contribute).

Usage

risk_set_weights(X_time, obs_times, delta, kerval, h, weight, one_sided)

Arguments

X_time, obs_times, delta

Event times, observation times, event indicator.

kerval

Row weights from kernel_weights().

h, weight, one_sided

As for kernel_weights().

Value

A list with index (integer) and K (numeric matrix).

Details

The matrix has one row per distinct event time, not per data row, because every row of a subject shares the subject's event time.
